newsitem.title: USA: IMM marks and yen end up as dollar rally stalled.
newsitem.headline: IMM marks and yen end up as dollar rally stalled.

text.p: Key IMM currency futures finished higher as the dollar's recent strong rally took a breather.
Traders said robust German economic data and talk of potential for a Japanese official rate rise dampened the dollar and drove gains in key currencies.

March mark reversed nearly all of Wednesday's losses and put a bit more distance between it and the contract low. One trading floor currency desk manager pegged a band of resistance for March from $0.5970 to $0.5980.
March yen rallied to a 1-1/2-week high at $0.008204.

In yen, traders focused on a recent rise in the average unsecured call rate above the 0.50 percent discount rate. Some said it could be a sign that higher official rates are not out of the question. Others pointed to the announcement that Japanese public-sector firms may purchase land related to failed housing loan companies.

A report of an interview recorded Monday with Bundesank President Hans Tietmeyer also kept a floor under mark futures. Tietmeyer said in the interview taped for broadcast in Hungary that he was against any further dollar rise against the mark.
Several traders said currency gains were mostly a function of dollar profit-taking and of dollar bulls looking for a setback before buying.
"It's still the idea that it's dollar bulls and they're looking for lower levels to buy the dollar again," one IMM trader said. "There are still huge dollar bulls."
Still, one analyst said the dollar was vulnerable to more of a pullback.
"I think the market trades like it's still long and there might be people who will get pushed out," he said. "This market is long and vulnerable."
He said March yen could rally to $0.008350 to $0.008400 before this dollar pullback is over.
Most U.S. data was largely ignored in the currency pits, though some said a strong Philadelphia Fed index may have aided currency gains early.
The Philly Fed business activity index rose to 17.4 in February from 11.3 in January, much higher than the 10.0 estimate.
Latest U.S. weekly jobless claims rose 1,000 to 309,000 in the latest week, and January housing starts rose 2.0 percent to a 1.35 million annual rate.
Traders said sterling futures trading was brisk early in the day, when sell stops were hit at 1.6100.
Traders said peso options activity was brisk.

At the end of pit trade, March yen was up $0.000117 to $0.008179, marks rose $0.0037 to $0.5940, Swiss francs rose $0.0037 to $0.6790, sterling fell $0.0050 to $1.6102, Can dollars fell $0.0006 to $0.7358 and Aussie dollars rose $0.0047 to $0.7722.
